propositions: Code review currently lacks a concurrency criterion to detect data races and synchronization violations, leaving only security (TOCTOU) and performance (stampede/pool exhaustion) overlays.

The concurrency overlay uses a two-tier deterministic lexical trigger: a committed high-precision tier firing on explicit synchronization primitives (Lock, flock, RwLock), and a project-extensible noisy tier in .rebar/criteria_routing.json for repo-specific patterns like git-index unlocked twins and lockfile TOCTOU.

The committed tier deliberately excludes the modal unlocked-twin race class (raw git rm+git commit, getmtime-then-remove on index.lock) to maintain portability, with project-level configuration required to catch repo-specific races.

The concurrency overlay must ship as advisory (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) and integrate into the base reviewer's overlay catalog for Pass-1 escalation without model-emitted severity.

The overlay must enable a project to extend trigger vocabulary through .rebar/criteria_routing.json without code changes, demonstrated by rebar's own dogfood configuration catching its four corpus bugs.
